clause0_repair.was: FixtureCases.test_fixture_covers_the_whole_class asserted that the fixture's case ids contained a tuple of ids the TEST FILE ITSELF declared: `REQUIRED_CASES = ("key-position-map-key", "nested-map-key", ... "collision-hold-approved-lyrics")` then `ids = [case["id"] for case in self.cases]; for wanted in self.REQUIRED_CASES: self.assertIn(wanted, ids)`. Nothing derived coverage from the payload, the catalogue or the compiler, so the test's own declaration was the oracle. Measured: with all nine cases keeping their ids and every `inject` emptied to {}, the check still passed.
clause0_repair.now: It asserts the property on the injected BYTES. For each case it deep-merges `case["inject"]` onto a real envelope, then re-derives from that payload which clause-0 dimensions are actually present: case variants and punctuation variants are read from the raw spellings against the catalogue's own display names; key-position, list-value, instruction-value and nested-position are read from the walker's paths; negative-key, negative-list-value and negative-instruction are read from the field name plus a negation cue in the text; approved-content is read from the protected-path predicate. Every one of the ten REQUIRED_DIMENSIONS must be witnessed, and each id that names a dimension the bytes do not show is a failure. The id is now a claim the bytes must confirm, never the oracle.
